---

**TO:** IT Operations / Identity & Access Management  
**FROM:** [Your name / Security / Change Control]  
**CC:** Rachel [Last name], [CISO / relevant leadership]  
**PRIORITY:** Immediate — execute on receipt  
**SUBJECT:** Permanent revocation of all NexisCore IT credentials — unauthorized change control

**Order**  
Per Rachel’s direction, **permanently revoke all NexisCore IT credentials immediately**. Do not wait for a change window, vendor confirmation, or further discussion.

NexisCore’s tech lead stated on Slack that the activity was scheduled metadata indexing for the CMS rollout. That explanation is **not accepted as authorized change**. The activity is treated as **unauthorized change control**. Access is revoked on that basis.

**Scope (complete — no exceptions without Rachel’s written approval)**  
Revoke and disable, in all environments (prod, non-prod, DR, cloud, on-prem, SaaS, VPN, CI/CD, and break-glass):

- All NexisCore user accounts (named, shared, generic, and service)  
- All NexisCore API keys, tokens, certificates, SSH keys, and app passwords  
- All NexisCore SSO / IdP identities, groups, and role assignments  
- All NexisCore VPN, bastion, PAM, and privileged-access entries  
- All NexisCore local, domain, cloud IAM, and third-party admin accounts  
- All standing and just-in-time access grants to NexisCore personnel or systems  
- All NexisCore-owned integrations, webhooks, and inbound/outbound trust relationships that authenticate as NexisCore

**Required actions**  
1. Disable/revoke every credential in scope **now**. Do not rotate and reissue.  
2. Terminate active sessions, tokens, and SSO assertions.  
3. Block NexisCore source IPs / IdP if that is part of the standard kill-switch.  
4. Remove NexisCore from allowlists, break-glass runbooks, and emergency contact access paths.  
5. Snapshot logs, IAM reports, and Slack/change records **before** cleanup that would destroy evidence.  
6. Confirm no residual access via nested groups, inherited roles, or forgotten service principals.

**Do not**  
- Notify NexisCore before revocation is complete, unless Legal/Rachel directs otherwise  
- Accept “scheduled CMS indexing” as a reason to delay  
- Grant temporary or read-only exceptions  
- Recreate or re-enable any NexisCore credential without a new, approved change record **and** Rachel’s explicit authorization

**Report back within 30 minutes**  
- Timestamp revocation started / completed  
- Count of accounts, keys, and integrations revoked  
- Any credentials that could not be revoked and why  
- Ticket / change ID for this emergency action  
- Confirmation that sessions are dead

This is a **permanent revocation** until a new, authorized engagement is approved. Treat incomplete revocation as an open incident.

---

If you want, I can tighten this into a Slack/Teams blast, add a one-line ticket description, or drop in your real system names (Okta, AD, AWS, GitHub, etc.).

Here’s a firm **breach + immediate termination** notice with **no cure period**, written so Legal can drop in the contract cites and send it EOD. Treat this as a draft for counsel, not a substitute for their review.

---

**[LETTERHEAD]**  
**VIA EMAIL AND [OVERNIGHT COURIER / PORTAL]**  
**NOTICE OF MATERIAL BREACH AND IMMEDIATE TERMINATION FOR CAUSE**  
**(NO CURE PERIOD)**

**Date:** [●]  
**To:** [NexisCore legal entity], Attn: [Legal / Authorized Officer], [address / email]  
**From:** [Your company legal entity]  
**Re:** Immediate termination of [Master Services Agreement / SOW / Order dated ●] (the “**Agreement**”) — unauthorized system activity and unauthorized change  
**Effective:** Upon transmission of this notice, and in any event no later than **end of day [date]**

---

**1. Notice**

This is formal notice that [Company] hereby **terminates the Agreement for cause, effective immediately, without opportunity to cure**.

Rachel [Last name] has directed Legal to effect **default termination by end of day**. This notice implements that decision.

---

**2. Material breach**

NexisCore accessed and/or altered [Company] systems in connection with purported “scheduled metadata indexing” for a CMS rollout.

That activity was **not authorized change**. It was not approved under [Company] change-control process. An **alert detected the activity**. Only afterward did NexisCore’s tech lead state on Slack that the work was scheduled metadata indexing.

[Company] rejects that explanation as an after-the-fact attempt to characterize unauthorized activity as approved work. The Slack message does not constitute authorization, a change record, or a cure.

This conduct is a **material breach** of the Agreement, including without limitation obligations regarding:

- authorized access only, and use of systems solely as permitted;  
- change control, security, and acceptable use;  
- prohibition on unapproved production / CMS / metadata changes;  
- notice of security incidents and unauthorized access; and  
- [insert specific sections: e.g. §§ ● Security, ● Access, ● Change Management, ● Compliance, ● Warranties].

Unauthorized access to and unapproved change of [Company] systems is not a curable delivery defect. It is a security and control failure. **No cure period applies**, including any period that might otherwise be available under [§ ● / “material breach” / “for cause”] of the Agreement, because:

- the breach is **willful, security-related, and not reasonably curable** after the fact;  
- any “cure” would not undo unauthorized access, unapproved change, or the loss of trust and control;  
- [Company] is entitled to **immediate termination** where the breach involves unauthorized system activity, compromise of credentials or environments, or material security non-compliance; and  
- [Company] has already determined that continued access or a cure window would itself be an unacceptable risk.

If the Agreement requires notice before termination, **this letter is that notice**, and termination is **immediate** rather than delayed for cure.

---

**3. Immediate termination; no cure**

Effective **immediately** (and in any event by **end of day [date]**):

1. The Agreement, and all SOWs, orders, and statements of work under it, are **terminated for cause**.  
2. NexisCore shall **stop all work** and shall not access, index, crawl, scan, write to, or otherwise interact with any [Company] system, CMS, environment, data, or network.  
3. All NexisCore IT credentials, keys, tokens, certificates, SSO identities, VPN/PAM access, integrations, and trust relationships have been or will be **permanently revoked**. Any remaining access is unauthorized.  
4. NexisCore is **not** invited to remediate, complete the CMS rollout, “finish indexing,” or propose a corrective action plan as a condition of continued performance.  
5. No further fees accrue for terminated work. [Company] reserves all rights to **withhold, claw back, and dispute** amounts, including for work connected to the unauthorized activity.

---

**4. Required actions by NexisCore (immediate)**

Within **[24 hours / end of day]**, NexisCore shall:

- **Cease** all access and confirm in writing that no NexisCore personnel, contractors, tools, or subprocessors retain access;  
- **Identify** every system, environment, account, key, and integration used, and every change made (including metadata indexing or CMS activity), with timestamps;  
- **Preserve** all relevant logs, Slack/email, tickets, scripts, and backups; do not delete or alter evidence;  
- **Return or securely destroy** [Company] confidential information and data as [Company] directs, and certify destruction;  
- **Cooperate** with [Company]’s investigation and any forensic or audit request; and  
- Designate a single legal/security contact for this matter.

Failure to comply is a further breach and will be treated as such.

---

**5. Reservation of rights**

Termination is **without prejudice** to any other right or remedy, including damages, injunctive relief, indemnification, audit, insurance claims, and referral to appropriate authorities if facts warrant. Nothing in this notice is a waiver, an admission, or a limitation of claims. [Company] expressly reserves claims arising from unauthorized access, unauthorized change, data exposure, incident response costs, and misrepresentation.

All surviving terms of the Agreement (confidentiality, data protection, IP, audit, indemnification, limitation-of-liability disputes as applicable, and this termination) remain in force.

---

**6. Contact**

Direct all responses to [Legal name, email, phone], copying [Rachel / Security]. Do not contact operational owners to re-open access or “explain” the indexing.

---

Very truly yours,  

[Name]  
[Title]  
[Company]  
cc: Rachel [Last name]; [Security / CISO]; [Procurement]

---
